name: Protected Audience (FLEDGE, retired)
plain: Browser run ad auctions for retargeting. Retirement announced Oct 2025; removal rolling out to 100% in Oct 2026.
meaning: Let advertisers store interest groups in the browser and run an on-device auction, keeping the audience list local. Joins fell almost 100x per the Chrome team. Chrome 144 deprecated it; staged removal on stable reaches 100% from Oct 26 2026.

access.persistence: Interest groups last up to 30 days, renewable
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

chrome.note: Removal rolling out from 152 and fully on by 2026-10-26

limits.headline: Can't run ads in Chrome based on your interests, since the plan was retired
limits.user_action: Nothing. It used to happen inside the browser during an ad auction
can: Have stored ad interest groups in the browser
Have run an ad auction on your device
Have shown a retargeted ad without sharing your history
cannot: Run in Chrome after removal reaches everyone in October 2026
Work in Edge, Firefox or Safari
Share your interests outside the browser
Replace cookies for all ad needs

story.what_it_is: Chrome ad auctions that ran in your browser for retargeting. Retired and being removed.

marketing.name: Protected Audience
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitched it as retargeting where interest groups stay in the browser and auctions run on device.

story.for_you: You may have seen retargeted ads picked by your browser, not a server. The shop that you visited added you to a group on your device. An auction ran locally. It is being removed in late 2026.
story.for_makers: It was Google's plan to keep retargeting after cookies. Few advertisers joined, and the Chrome team said joins fell almost 100 times. So Google retired it in 2025.

use_cases.example: You look at a tent. Your browser adds you to a group, and later an ad for the tent wins a local auction.
An ad network ran an on device auction among shops that want to reach you.
A game studio kept a group of lapsed players on the browser, to win them back with an ad.
A publisher sold a slot that ran an auction on device, with ad picks made from private interests.
Teams measured the groups, but small groups gave poor data.
A hotel site added visitors to a group that bid on a trip ad later.

risks: Auction results were hard to audit

technical_bounds: Interest groups limited to 30 days with refresh
Bidding code could not log to the network
Ads rendered in fenced frames without leaking identity to the page
Chrome only; other browsers declined to ship

abuse: Large interest group collection by many adtech scripts

history.change: Removal started at 1% of stable; paused at 10% until Oct 12; 100% from Oct 26 2026 (per blink-dev summary)
